verdict.reasoning: Patient states: "I've been having this blinding headache for a few days" and later confirms "that was three days ago," indicating an acute, severe headache for 3 days.
Patient says headache started three days ago and rates severity: "I guess it's mostly eight, and then it comes down to maybe a five" with ibuprofen; duration and pain scores match.
Patient: "I woke up one morning with a headache, and that was three days ago... kind of all the time... I still have it still there," supporting onset upon waking 3 days ago and persistence.
Patient: "When I take ibuprofen, it gets a bit better... but then I still have it still there," indicating only partial relief and not complete resolution.
Patient: "It's kind of all over, but I feel like over. My right eye is a bit stronger," supporting diffuse pain with right eye more involved.
Patient: "Lights definitely make me more sensitive. I don't really like strong lights" is consistent with photophobia.
Patient reports: "I think I get this shooting light sometimes... Just a bit of a weird kind of vision," supporting intermittent shooting lights in vision.
When asked about nausea/vomiting, patient says: "No, I'm feeling a bit sick, but no vomiting," which implies nausea is present though vomiting is absent; fact claims denial of both.
Patient: "No, I didn't [check temperature], but I don't really feel feverish or anything," supporting that fever is not reported.
Patient: "Yeah, I'm sleeping" and "No, no, but I can wake up with it in the morning," indicating normal sleep, not waking at night, but present on waking and persisting.

Patient: "I find it quite difficult to get through my daily activities" and "couldn't really manage to do it all the time... I just stopped in the morning because I couldn't focus," showing interference with activities and work.
Patient: "Sometimes when I stand up quickly, I get a bit of a stabbing pain or if I turn my head, I kind of feel like something is moving inside," directly supports positional stabbing pain.
Patient: "Yeah, actually had one [eye check] recently and nothing changed my vision," indicating recent eye exam and no vision change.
Patient: "I think I only had the abdominal pain when I was younger, but no cause was found and that went away," matches childhood abdominal pain without identified etiology.
After describing childhood abdominal pain, patient adds "but that's the only thing I know of," indicating otherwise unremarkable past medical history.
Patient: "Just the pill." When asked which one: "Marcelone" and "About a year ago," confirming use and timing of this combined oral contraceptive.
Patient: "No, I don't think so" re side effects and "No, because this headache is just very recent. Nothing really changes" regarding change in headaches, matching the claim.
Patient mentions ibuprofen multiple times for headache: "it just went away with ibuprofen" and "When I take ibuprofen, it gets a bit better," showing use for headache relief.
When asked about allergies, patient replies: "No," supporting no known allergies.
Patient: "my mum suffers from, like, she has migraines... quite bad migraines. She's like. Has the vomiting and everything," confirming maternal history of migraine.
When asked who they live with, patient says: "Just by myself," indicating they live alone.
In response to smoking: patient says: "No," confirming non-smoker status.
On alcohol: patient says: "Probably like three beers once a Week," matching about three beers per week.
Patient: "I work from home" and repeats regarding recent days, confirming work from home.
Transcript contains no vital signs or physical exam findings; only history is taken and future exam planned, so noting no documented vitals/exam is accurate.
Patient: "Yeah, actually had one [eye check] recently and nothing changed my vision," which describes a recent normal eye exam without vision changes.

Doctor states: "it could possibly be a migraine type headache" and history includes acute severe headache, photophobia, visual phenomena, and note that ongoing for 3 days so further exam needed; this aligns with migraine-type pattern while not excluding secondary causes.

Doctor discusses pill and migraines: "Because if we do think it's a migraine, then you would have to change your pill... that pill, if you were having regular migraines with flashing lights... it wouldn't be suitable to stay on that pill," showing review of contraception given possible migraine pattern.
Patient describes missing and cutting back on work from home due to headache: "couldn't really manage" and "stopped in the morning because I couldn't focus," confirming significant functional impact.

Doctor plans: "we probably should book you into an appointment to get an examination... we should do a neurological examination, look at the back of your eyes as well" and "book an appointment with the support team"; there is no mention of ophthalmology follow-up or documentation of results, only a GP/clinic exam including fundoscopy.

Doctor: "I can prescribe you something similar to ibuprofen, but a bit stronger... and you can take paracetamol at the same time" and later "take it with food," matching a stronger NSAID plus paracetamol with food.

Transcript does not advise continuing ibuprofen conditionally; instead, doctor prescribes an alternative: "something similar to ibuprofen, but a bit stronger, which you can take instead of ibuprofen," contradicting the idea of continuing ibuprofen.

Doctor advises: "if... your headache is getting unbearable, getting worse or changing, then... you should go to AE" and to call for advice; no mention is made of specific triggers like focal deficits, fever, slurred speech, weakness, or confusion.

Doctor: "When you have an examination with us, we'll check your blood pressure as well, just to make sure your pill is still appropriate for you. Because if we do think it's a migraine, then you would have to change your pill..." which matches BP measurement and reassessment of pill suitability in context of migraine-like symptoms.

There is no counseling in the transcript about avoiding triggers, maintaining hydration, ensuring rest, or encouraging follow-up beyond scheduling the exam and AE advice; these educational elements are not discussed.
